rationale.complete: Round 1 done: dated predictions, synthetic validation at real reply structures (with an amendment before the real run), 32 replication periods (43 units), three natives (G12, G26, G23), scorecard, 190 estimates rows, confirmatory script frozen and dry-run. Holdout not run; two natives underpowered.
rationale.faithfulness: The settlement switch-off in #12 beats team permutation, two-way agent effects, a heat field and remanence, with soft and hard labels. The competition contrast beats the prize-free set but rests on an unvalidated stance subtype in four regime-I periods, and no rival-specific antagonism appears outside #12. Scorecard all 1s except I.
rationale.usefulness: A monitor-level rule: stance antagonism tracks the incentive state, so settling a prize ends it within minutes and rival roles without a single winner do not create feuds. Effects are small outside assigned debates.

one_line: Settling a prize switches assigned antagonism off within minutes; open competition raises disagreement room-wide, not between rivals.

models.note: Antagonism follows the prize field; no remanent pair coupling
Two-camp order only with assigned sides

v2.scope: #12 (primary design), 4 competition vs 26 prize-free units; natives G12, G26, G23
